ARR01-C.name: Do not apply the sizeof operator to a pointer when taking the size of an array

ARR02-C.name: Explicitly specify array bounds, even if implicitly defined by an initializer

ARR30-C.name: Do not form or use out-of-bounds pointers or array subscripts

ARR32-C.name: Ensure size arguments for variable length arrays are in a valid range

ARR36-C.name: Do not subtract or compare two pointers that do not refer to the same array

ARR38-C.name: Guarantee that library functions do not form invalid pointers

ARR39-C.name: Do not add or subtract a scaled integer to a pointer

CON31-C.name: Do not destroy a mutex while it is locked

CON32-C.name: Prevent data races when accessing bit-fields from multiple threads

CON33-C.name: Avoid race conditions when using library functions

CON40-C.name: Do not refer to an atomic variable twice in an expression

CON43-C.name: Do not allow data races in multithreaded code

DCL06-C.name: Use meaningful symbolic constants to represent literal values in program logic

DCL10-C.name: Maintain the contract between the writer and caller of variadic functions

DCL30-C.name: Declare objects with appropriate storage durations

ENV01-C.name: Do not make assumptions about the size of an environment variable

ENV02-C.name: Beware of multiple environment variables with the same effective name

ENV03-C.name: Sanitize the environment when invoking external programs

ENV32-C.name: All exit handlers must return normally

ERR00-C.name: Adopt and implement a consistent and comprehensive error-handling policy

ERR07-C.name: Prefer functions that support error checking over equivalent functions that don't

ERR30-C.name: Set errno to zero before calling a library function known to set errno,  and check errno only after the function returns a value indicating failure

ERR33-C.name: Detect and handle standard library errors

ERR34-C.name: Detect errors when converting a string to a number

EXP00-C.name: Use parentheses for precedence of operation

EXP05-C.name: Do not cast away a const qualification

EXP08-C.name: Ensure pointer arithmetic is used correctly

EXP30-C.name: Do not depend on the order of evaluation for side effects

EXP37-C.name: Call functions with the correct number and type of arguments

EXP39-C.name: Do not access a variable through a pointer of an incompatible type

EXP45-C.name: Do not perform assignments in selection statements

EXP46-C.name: Do not use a bitwise operator with a Boolean-like operand

FIO01-C.name: Be careful using functions that use file names for identification

FIO02-C.name: Canonicalize path names originating from untrusted sources

FIO05-C.name: Identify files using multiple file attributes

FIO06-C.name: Create files with appropriate access permissions

FIO15-C.name: Ensure that file operations are performed in a secure directory

FIO30-C.name: Exclude user input from format strings

FIO32-C.name: Do not perform operations on devices that are only appropriate for files

FIO34-C.name: Distinguish between characters read from a file and EOF or WEOF

FIO37-C.name: Do not assume that fgets() or fgetws() returns a nonempty string when successful

FIO39-C.name: Do not alternately input and output from a stream without an intervening flush or positioning call

FIO42-C.name: Close files when they are no longer needed

FIO46-C.name: Do not access a closed file

FLP03-C.name: Detect and handle floating point errors

FLP32-C.name: Prevent or detect domain and range errors in math functions

FLP34-C.name: Ensure that floating point conversions are within range of the new type

INT05-C.name: Do not use input functions to convert character data if they cannot handle all possible inputs

INT07-C.name: Use only explicitly signed or unsigned char type for numeric values

INT13-C.name: Use bitwise operators only on unsigned operands

INT15-C.name: Use intmax_t or uintmax_t for formatted IO on programmer-defined integer types

INT18-C.name: Evaluate integer expressions in a larger size before comparing or assigning to that size

INT30-C.name: Ensure that unsigned integer operations do not wrap

INT31-C.name: Ensure that integer conversions do not result in lost or misinterpreted data

INT32-C.name: Ensure that operations on signed integers do not result in overflow

INT33-C.name: Ensure that division and remainder operations do not result in divide-by-zero errors

INT34-C.name: Do not shift an expression by a negative number of bits or by greater than or equal  to the number of bits that exist in the operand

INT35-C.name: Evaluate integer expressions in a larger size before comparing or assigning to that size

INT36-C.name: Converting a pointer to integer or integer to pointer

MEM00-C.name: Allocate and free memory in the same module, at the same level of abstraction

MEM01-C.name: Store a new value in pointers immediately after free()

MEM03-C.name: Clear sensitive information stored in reusable resources returned for reuse

MEM04-C.name: Do not perform zero length allocations

MEM06-C.name: Ensure that sensitive data is not written out to disk

MEM07-C.name: Ensure that the arguments to calloc(), when multiplied, do not wrap

MEM10-C.name: Define and use a pointer validation function

MEM31-C.name: Free dynamically allocated memory when no longer needed

MEM35-C.name: Allocate sufficient memory for an object

MSC00-C.name: Compile cleanly at high warning levels

MSC06-C.name: Be aware of compiler optimization when dealing with sensitive data

MSC14-C.name: Do not introduce unnecessary platform dependencies

MSC15-C.name: Do not depend on undefined behavior

MSC30-C.name: Do not use the rand() function for generating pseudorandom numbers

MSC37-C.name: Ensure that control never reaches the end of a non-void function

POS01-C.name: Check for the existence of links when dealing with files

POS02-C.name: Follow the principle of least privilege

POS34-C.name: Do not call putenv() with a pointer to an automatic variable as the argument

POS35-C.name: Avoid race conditions while checking for the existence of a symbolic link

POS36-C.name: Observe correct revocation order while relinquishing privileges

POS37-C.name: Ensure that privilege relinquishment is successful

POS48-C.name: Do not unlock or destroy another POSIX thread's mutex

POS54-C.name: Detect and handle POSIX library errors

PRE09-C.name: Do not replace secure functions with less secure functions

SIG00-C.name: Mask signals handled by noninterruptible signal handlers

SIG30-C.name: Call only asynchronous-safe functions within signal handlers

SIG31-C.name: Do not access or modify shared objects in signal handlers

SIG34-C.name: Do not call signal() from within interruptible signal handlers

STR02-C.name: Sanitize data passed to complex subsystems

STR03-C.name: Do not inadvertently truncate a null-terminated byte string

STR06-C.name: Do not assume that strtok() leaves the parse string unchanged

STR31-C.name: Guarantee that storage for strings has sufficient space for character data and the null terminator

STR32-C.name: Do not pass a non-null-terminated character sequence to a library function that expects a string

STR34-C.name: Cast characters to unsigned types before converting to larger integer sizes

STR37-C.name: Arguments to character handling functions must be representable as an unsigned char

WIN30-C.name: Properly pair allocation and deallocation functions
